primarySourceDescription: US Army Command and General Staff College digitized 2-page Belgian Air Force Order of Battle, dated 10 May 1940; table cites E.C. Weal and J.A. Weal, Combat Aircraft of World War Two (1977). Despite US Army archive hosting, NUMBERS derive from secondary book, not contemporary unit registers.
alternativeSourceDescription: Specialist secondary compilation distinguishing prewar/base assignment versus wartime dispersal sites; contains contradictions to US CGSC table in unit designations and aircraft allocations. All alternative sites are candidates, NOT independently verified historical airfield coordinates.
officialCampaignStatement: Belgian government wartime/postwar official account states German attacks on 10 May destroyed MORE THAN HALF of Belgian Air Force machines on the ground. This is qualitative, not a number of confirmed losses or a specific count of planes surviving after 10 May.
warnings: The 182 aircraft are from 16 selected combat/army-cooperation squadron rows; air training, reserves, communications and anti-aircraft detachments were not included. This is NOT a verified national all-aircraft-on-hand number.
Squadron 'fighter regiment' includes older Fairey Fox aircraft, so DO NOT interpret all 79 aircraft as equivalent modern interceptors or as 79 serviceable airplanes.
There is no serviceability count and no proven aircraft-versus-pilot matching in this OOB.

Several unit names and equipment counts disagree with alternate Nevington compilation, which itself contains serious typographic and historical errors: alternatives require better original Belgian sources.
The CGSC printed base strings may refer to prewar/administrative bases, not dispersed wartime airfields. Two stations named per unit do not mean the unit was simultaneously at two bases.
Unverified candidate bases have no coordinates and must not be mapped on 10 May 1940 as settled facts.
